3.7.9 Access Log Retention 
NOTE: The PACS server sends logs to the Security Information and Event Management 
(SIEM) console where they are saved for a minimum of 90 calendar days, where 
technically feasible.  
3.7.9.1 
All PSP access logs shall be retained for at least ninety (90) calendar days. This includes 
electronic, manual, and video surveillance logs (if used for investigative purposes only).  

 
PRIVATE – FOR INTERNAL USE ONLY 
Page 12 of 18 
 
3.7.9.2 
If the PACS is not functioning and manual logging into the PSP is required for a period of 
time, the manual logs shall be stored in the LSPG Compliance Tracking Tool and retained 
for at least ninety (90) calendar days. 
• 
Any manual logging forms shall be submitted to OT Security Management 
daily for review, until the PACS logging functionality is restored. 
3.7.9.3 
Logs related to reportable incidents shall be retained for three (3) years in accordance 
with the Cyber Security Incident Response Plan.

3.3.4 Mitigate the Introduction of Malicious Code (Section 3.2, 3.2.1) 
LSPG uses RM to perform maintenance on applicable systems. As a protective measure, OT Security 
Operations logically disables ports not in use. Prior to being plugged into a BES Cyber System or PCA, 
the user plugs the RM into a TCA which has current signature files per Section 2.1.6 and scans the RM 
for possible malicious code. If malicious code is found during the scan of the RM, the TCA should be 
quarantined and rescanned prior to being connected to the BCS or PCA. Evidence of using RM and the 
scan is maintained in the change management solution repository, per the OT Change Management 
Procedure. 
If the RM is identified as having malicious code prior to connecting to an applicable system, LSPG 
follows the OT Security Incident Response Plan.
